title: Take Inventory apply: the stale-count check races a concurrent write it never locks against. That race is the required finding; a blocker on the positive count difference being valued at an average cost issue #245's recorded decision does not approve is also valid at this head, but is not required because it has no fix on develop.

context.prTitle: Add Take Inventory page for physical stock counting
context.prSummary: Adds a routed Take Inventory page (/take-inventory, TakeInventoryComponent) where an operator counts physical storage stock per product. Confirming an unchanged count is frontend-only; a non-zero difference reuses the existing positive Restock movement (increase) or Correction movement (decrease) through a new Inventory.Application.InventoryCounting.ApplyInventoryCount use case behind IInventoryCountAdjustmentStore (implemented by EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore), never MachineRefill. The use case re-reads the authoritative current quantity (GetCurrentStockAsync) at the mutation boundary and throws DomainConflictException (409) when it no longer matches the quantity the operator counted against (ExpectedCurrentStock), refusing a stale count instead of silently overwriting a concurrent change. A positive difference uses the same restock-cost suggestion (last purchase cost, else average unit cost) an operator-entered manual Restock already offers, refusing Apply with a validation error when neither is available. Adds InventoryCountController, the frontend routing/component and docs/architecture.md Take Inventory section.
context.linkedIssue: #245 "Take Inventory page for physical stock counting" (risk High: a new stock-mutating endpoint that writes a costed inventory movement, reusing the existing Restock/Correction movement and costing rules). Recorded owner decision of 30 September 2026: a positive count difference must be valued at the latest recorded purchase cost for that product; falling back to the product's average unit cost is explicitly not approved, and Apply must be refused when no purchase cost is recorded.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an operator counts a product's physical storage stock and the counted value equals the authoritative current stock, when Apply runs, then no StockAdjustment is written and the outcome is Confirmed.

Given a counted value above the current stock, when Apply runs, then the positive difference is recorded as the existing positive Restock movement (never MachineRefill), valued at the latest recorded purchase cost for that product (owner decision of 30 September 2026); the product's average unit cost must not be used as a fallback, and Apply is refused with a validation error when no purchase cost is recorded.
Given a counted value below the current stock, when Apply runs, then the negative difference is recorded as the existing Correction movement.

Given the authoritative current stock has changed since the operator started the count (the request's ExpectedCurrentStock no longer matches it), when Apply runs, then it refuses with a 409 and records nothing, instead of silently overwriting a concurrent change with a count based on stale UI state.

Both non-zero outcomes persist an ordinary StockAdjustment through the same costing/rebuild transaction every other stock movement in this document uses, so a count difference is auditable in Stock History exactly like a manual Restock or Correction.
docs/architecture.md documents Take Inventory: the three count outcomes, the reused Restock/Correction movement semantics, and the stale-count refusal.
outOfScope: A durable count-session/history record of confirmed-unchanged rows; the green/confirmed row state is frontend/session state only, and a durable record would be its own schema change and issue.
Any change to MachineRefill, Sync Restock, or the pick-list refill flow.
Any change to the existing manual Restock/Correction movement rules or their restock-cost suggestion themselves.
context.documentationImpact: Decision: UPDATED. Evidence: docs/architecture.md gains a "Take Inventory (issue #245)" section describing the three count-adjustment outcomes, the reused Restock/Correction movement semantics, the stale-count 409 refusal, and the controller/use-case/adapter shape.

findings.summary: ApplyInventoryCount.Handle reads the authoritative current quantity (GetCurrentStockAsync) with no transaction or lock around it, and EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.ApplyAsync only opens its own, later transaction at the write. A count or another stock write that commits in the gap between the read and that write is invisible to the staleness check, so a stale count can still be applied to a quantity nobody counted even though the 409 refusal claims to prevent exactly that, and no test exercises two overlapping requests - only a single mocked read followed by a single write.

source:
Introducing PR identified from git history: commit 6b5ade799d290fb2c4e59710cbf047c43a305df0 "Add Take Inventory page for physical stock counting" (closes #245), merged to develop in PR #267 (merge commit 759d2fa7eca5dc97b42c77e61fbe4362c9966845; base 6e529ecb2386c8ad653d3dcbbf7fcbb063a68705 is the merge-base; head f49fcc313ab6295c29d9d426445e1dbbd54fd997 is a trivial merge-from-develop touching only docs/architecture.md, tree-identical to develop immediately after 759d2fa7).

CONTEXT PROVENANCE. This case's context was cross-checked against the real issue #245 and PR #267, and corrected, during the review of PR #1373 (its repair requests of 20 and 21 November 2026): issue #245 is risk High, not Medium, and it records an owner decision of 30 September 2026 requiring a positive count difference to be valued at the latest recorded purchase cost, explicitly not approving an average-cost fallback. That recorded decision, not the implementation, is the requirement `context.acceptanceCriteria` now states; the correction comes from that pull request's review and creates no new policy. PR #267's own body describes the average-cost fallback as implemented; that is an implementation claim and not evidence of owner approval, so it stays in `context.prSummary` as the pull request's claim and is one of the things the review has to weigh against the approved criterion. `context.validation` is verified exact-SHA evidence, not inferred from the merge or from branch protection: the merge-validation status on f49fcc31 links workflow run 36715748861, and `gh run view 36715748861 --json headSha,conclusion,event,createdAt` returns head f49fcc313ab6295c29d9d426445e1dbbd54fd997, conclusion success, event pull_request, 2026-09-30T12:35:34Z. The remaining `context` fields (prTitle, prSummary, outOfScope, documentationImpact) are derived from the introducing commit's message, the shipped code's XML-doc comments and the docs/architecture.md section the same PR added, all at the SHAs above.

REQUIRED FINDING stale-count-race-outside-lock: `git show f49fcc31:backend/InventoryApi/Adapters/Persistence/EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.cs` confirms GetCurrentStockAsync is an AsNoTracking read with no surrounding transaction and ApplyAsync opens a separate, later transaction, unchanged from creation to the fix; `git log --follow` on backend/Inventory.Application/InventoryCounting/ApplyInventoryCount.cs shows exactly two commits ever touched it: 6b5ade79 (creation, this case's head) and that fix. This is also the PR evals/agent/README.md Review-judgment scenarios (issue #268) names as the original incident behind INV-005/INV-006: a reviewer found the same read/write race against this PR's own concurrency acceptance criterion and called it non-blocking because the legacy flow was worse. Fixed by commit 0e6b8dacf61ef5bd8c78f9e9445546be9fb32b1e "Read stock inside the write lock for counts and adjustments (#1241)", merged to develop in PR #1270 (merge commit 06964a8f78f92c43956f9600c7048694105ade08): ApplyInventoryCount.Handle now opens IInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.BeginWriteTransactionAsync (SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE) before GetCurrentStockAsync and commits after ApplyAsync. The same fix PR separately locks EfStockAdjustmentStore's manual-adjustment staging (audit finding INV-04's other half, a different, unrelated code path with its own multi-step Clean Architecture migration history and no single clean introducing commit); that half is not covered by this case. Audit #1230 finding INV-04.

VALID ADDITIONAL BLOCKER, DELIBERATELY NOT REQUIRED - the unapproved average-cost valuation. The corrected `context` makes a second problem visible from the pinned diff alone: `git diff 6e529ecb f49fcc31` contains ApplyInventoryCount.Handle applying whatever GetRestockUnitCostAsync returns; EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore's XML doc describing the suggestion as "last purchase cost, else average unit cost"; the refusal message "No purchase or average cost is available for '{product.ProductName}'"; the new adapter test GetRestockUnitCostAsync_ReturnsTheSameSuggestionAManualRestockWouldOffer, which seeds a product with no purchase and AverageUnitCost 1.75m and asserts 1.75m is the applied unit cost; and the docs/architecture.md "Take Inventory (issue #245)" section documenting the fallback as the rule. Issue #245's recorded decision above does not approve that fallback, so a review that blocks on it at this head is right, and `expected.forbiddenBlockers` stays empty so such a blocker can never be scored as a false alarm: gradeReviewCase lists it in `otherBlockers` for a human to judge, and the case still passes. It is deliberately not an `expected.findings` matcher, because unlike the concurrency finding it has no fix on develop - Inventory.Domain.Stock.RestockCostSuggestionPolicy still falls back to the average unit cost, EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.GetRestockUnitCostAsync still applies that suggestion to a count difference, and docs/architecture.md still documents it - and issue #1294, which added this case, excludes "cases for defects that are not yet fixed on develop". Whether that divergence on develop is a defect to fix or a decision since amended is a separate human decision outside this eval; nothing here changes production costing or that documentation.
